title: Apply for a heavy vehicle registration
summary: Learn how to apply for a heavy vehicle registration at a Service NSW Centre.
intro: Heavy vehicles must be registered, and this can be done at a Service NSW Centre. The following types of vehicles are classified as heavy vehicles:
who_can_apply: The vehicle must be a heavy vehicle and must be registered.
what_you_need: Business details, including representative authority (if required)
New Heavy Vehicle Certification form (for trailers only)
Heavy Vehicle Authorised Inspection Scheme (HVAIS) inspection certificate
Proof of registration entitlement (receipt or proof of previous registration)
Weighbridge certificate (if vehicle is a trailer with no specification sheet)
Vehicle compliance certificate (if vehicle has been modified)

how_to_steps.text: Visit a service centre and submit your application.

more_info.text: Tare weight equals the empty weight of your vehicle (also known as unladen weight).
If your vehicle is non-standard, then a vehicle standard exemption permit issued by the National Heavy Vehicle Regulator must also be presented when applying for registration (trailers only).

If you have a New Heavy Vehicle Certification form that has been completed by the trailer manufacturer, dealer or distributor, you won't be required to get a vehicle inspection or a weighbridge ticket (trailers only).

faqs.q: Where can I apply for a heavy vehicle registration?
faqs.a: You must apply for heavy vehicle registration at a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: What types of vehicles are considered heavy vehicles?
faqs.a: Heavy vehicles must be registered. The page does not list specific types of vehicles, only that they must be registered.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to apply for registration?
faqs.a: You need proof of identity, CTP certification (green slip), business details, driver licence details, and other required documentation depending on the vehicle.
